questions.q: What does Branson's childhood bike trip illustrate?
a: A taste for risk can be learned rather than inherited
Children should never be given directions
Physical challenges are the best business training
Parents should push children into entrepreneurship
questions.why: The first lesson says his parents deliberately gave him challenges, and the broader point is that you need not be born an entrepreneur.

questions.q: How did Virgin Atlantic get its start?
a: He chartered a plane and sold seats to stranded travelers
He bought an existing airline with family money
He won an airline in a business bet
He began with cargo flights between the islands
questions.why: When his flight was cancelled, Branson chartered a plane for 2,000 dollars and sold every seat for 39 dollars each.

questions.q: What does the summary say about how Branson handles his ventures?
a: He takes one adventure at a time and gives it everything
He runs many businesses simultaneously
He avoids new industries until an old one fails
He only invests in sectors he already understands
questions.why: The second lesson says he watches for the next opportunity but seizes one at a time, building each business before starting another.

questions.q: Why does Branson spot opportunities that others miss?
a: He practices creativity long before he needs it
He takes bigger financial risks than anyone else
He hires more creative advisors than rivals
He studies his competitors in great detail
questions.why: The third lesson says you cannot invent a solution on the spot unless you have practiced creativity well in advance.

questions.q: Which daily habit does the summary recommend for building creativity?
a: Writing down ten ideas every day
Reading one book every week
Drawing for twenty minutes each morning
Brainstorming with a group each week
questions.why: It cites James Altucher's practice of writing ten ideas a day as a great way to exercise creative muscles.
